I was camping in the mountains of Alberta once and we came down to a lake with a wooden bridge across it. It was around 8am, the air was crisp with chill, there's this guy with some kind of case standing alone on the bridge. We were higher up on the hill, the lake is surrounded on 3 sides with snow capped rocky mountains, the guy opens his case and takes out a cornet trumpet. My stop and watch, his trumpet gleams golden in the misty sunlight. I start grinning like a fool before he even plays the first note.

He plays Rhapsody in Blue. It echoes off the mountains and the notes almost skip off the water. The whole valley seems to just bathe in the acoustics of the sound. I'm covered in goosebumps just remembering it.

The guy finishes the song and puts away his cornet then walks across the bridge away from us and on his way. The whole experience was just so incredible and random. If we weren't out trying to get warmed up by taking the morning hike we'd have missed it. If we weren't out that morning he would have been playing alone, just for himself and the mountains, I'm still not sure he even knew we were there.

Great post, upvoted. I disagree with you on some points, so I hope you don't mind me bringing them up here.

We have examples of biology in nature that shows sterile people can still contribute to spreading their particular genes. How? Let's say I have a twin who is sterile. I'm fertile, as is my wife. If my twin joins my wife and me on our hunts, then we have a better chance of living and reproducing than the couple next door who only has 2 people. My twin, despite being sterile, improves the chances of his genes being spread because I share them with him, and my son biologically-speaking could be his son since he and I are twins.

Moving from that, a typical pair of siblings shares a lot of genes with one another. So the above situation applies for regular siblings, not just twins. This is why eusociality works. Now here's where it gets a bit convoluted:

Gay people don't just sit around all day. They do things, and most of those things improve their genetic fit within the gene pool. They contribute to charity to feed poor children (increasing the chances of those children's genes of reproducing) and work in industries that further human livelihood (improving genetic fit in innumerable ways). By simply spending money (something that animals don't do), gay humans play a part in maintaining an economy, where their fertile neighbors rely upon to make a living and propagate. Of course, they do things like give money and time to their relatives as well.

Now to tackle your last point, "gay couples can’t really do that to the full extent." I honestly don't think someone needs to do something to the full extent in order to count as being valid. I mean, if you want to say that fertility and reproduction to the full extent is the only way to be in line with "basic human instinct", then you should also have a problem with couples who only have 1 or 2 children. After all, the full extent is them keep rearing a dozen children until they become infertile, no?
